text:
mariam: FWIW I hit a weird SSL failure on Windows with AsyncClient on py3.11 today. Sync client OK.

mariam: Minimal repro: create venv, pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2 httpx certifi, run:
```python
# async_check.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient
async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-test")
    await c.chat.create(model="gptx-mini", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}])
asyncio.run(main())
```

mariam: Error: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: unable to get local issuer certificate. Setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi bundle fixes it, which suggests our async path is forcing cafile and ignoring the Windows store.

tao: That matches an earlier bug: passing cafile to create_default_context on Windows causes OpenSSL to not consult the platform store. Likely async transport sets cafile=certifi.where() unconditionally.

cli-bot: created issue SDK-8821: "Windows async client: cert file precedence causes verification failures" and assigned to @tao.

tao: Plan: add AsyncClient param use_system_certs, default behavior on Windows will prefer system store unless SSL_CERT_FILE explicitly set. Add unit tests and a short docs note. Will target 0.9.3 patch.

support: Please add a short support blurb: workaround = set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where(), and note to recommend use_system_certs once patch lands.

mariam: Thanks. Adding Windows py3.10/3.11 async test to CI matrix would help catch regressions.
